findings.source_passage: And on Mondays eight servants, including an extra gardener, toiled all day with mops and scrubbing-brushes …
findings.source_locator: early catalogue paragraph (after Rolls-Royce omnibus line)
findings.why_it_matters: The parenthetical "including an extra gardener" is a miniature punch-line that completes Nick’s comic inventory of excess; deleting it flattens the sentence’s rhythm and irony.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the parenthetical phrase verbatim within the sentence.

findings.source_passage: The last swimmers have come in from the beach now and are dressing upstairs; the cars from New York are parked five deep in the drive …
findings.why_it_matters: The clipped clause about the swimmers is part of Fitzgerald’s kinetic present-tense montage; cutting it breaks the cinematic pan from water to driveway and dulls the paragraph’s cadence.
findings.suggested_fix: Reinsert the swimmer clause exactly where it stands in the source.

findings.source_passage: “Ladies and gentlemen,” he cried. “At the request of Mr. Gatsby we are going to play for you Mr. Vladmir Tostoff’s latest work … He smiled with jovial condescension, and added: “Some sensation!”
findings.source_locator: orchestra-leader announcement before “Jazz History of the World”
findings.why_it_matters: The burlesque showman rhetoric (“Some sensation!”) is a tonal set-piece; replacing it with a one-sentence summary strips out Fitzgerald’s vaudeville patter and loses a recognizable comic beat.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full three-sentence announcement, keeping the direct quotation and stagey asides.

findings.source_passage: “I was brought by a woman named Roosevelt,” he continued. “Mrs. Claud Roosevelt. Do you know her? … I’ve been drunk for about a week now, and I thought it might sober me up to sit in a library.”
findings.source_locator: Owl-Eyes library scene, after “Who brought you?”
findings.why_it_matters: The rambling Roosevelt aside is characteristic Owl-Eyes comedy and a small class satire; dropping it shortens the exchange and blunts Nick’s portrait of drunken, name-dropping privilege.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Roosevelt lines in the Owl-Eyes speech.

findings.source_passage: —and no singing quartets were formed with Gatsby’s head for one link.
findings.why_it_matters: The quirky image of Gatsby as a potential human barbershop link is a final comic twist that underscores his isolation amid the revelry; cutting it mutes the irony.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert the missing clause at the end of the sentence, exactly as in the source.

summary: Five voice-driven set-pieces and punch-lines are trimmed or flattened; restore them to keep Fitzgerald’s rhythm and irony intact.
